newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAA says most departures on schedule Thurs.
newsitem.headline: SAA says most departures on schedule Thurs.

text.p: South African Airways (SAA) said conditions at local airports had improved on Thursday and most departures were on schedule despite a week-long go-slow by aviation technicians and engineers.
SAA on Wednesday locked out about 1,800 protesting South African Aviation Engineering and Allied Union (SAAEAU) members, delaying most flights.
"It is going much better today (Thursday). We have been able to schedule more flights. More aircrafts have been made available and many flights left on time," SAA spokesman Leon Els told Reuters.

The 2,200-strong SAAEAU applied for a court interdict on Wednesday to stop SAA from issuing letters to locked-out union members calling on them to agree to the airline's wage offer and end their week long work-to-rule protest action.
A court dismissed the application with costs.
Els said the lock-out was still in effect for those workers who would not sign the letter and a meeting was being planned with the union.
"The lock-out is still in position. We are waiting for figures on how many (workers), in light of the court ruling, are starting to return to work," Els said.
SAAEAU has declared a dispute with SAA for its refusal to offer a 25 percent wage rise. Management is offering a 10 percent increase plus a 20 percent productivity bonus.
SAA said the week-long go-slow by technicians and engineers had cost it about 40 million rand so far.
The union could not be reached for comment.
